parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Mission · the main urban area
Mission BC is an MLS® sub-area name. The City of Mission doesn’t publish a boundary for it.
The City’s Heritage Context Study describes Mission as 250 square kilometres in size, on the north bank of the Fraser River.

My working description, not an official boundary: the main urban area, from the Fraser River up through the central streets and the Cedar Valley growth area. On this site, listings tagged Mission BC are mainly on Cedar Street, Dewdney Trunk Road, Tunbridge Avenue, 3rd Avenue, Best Avenue and Cherry Avenue.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 18, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate since 2015. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Mission and Mission Public Schools (School District 75).
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations, flood rules and school catchments before you buy or sell.

blocks.text: West Coast Express and buses Mission City Station

parts.t: According to TransLink, the West Coast Express links Downtown Vancouver and Mission City on weekdays, running at the morning and evening rush hours. In the morning it goes westbound only, and in the afternoon and evening eastbound only
The West Coast Express page lists five westbound trains from Mission City, at 5:25, 5:55, 6:25, 6:55 and 7:25 a.m.
Buses connecting to Mission City Station, which is at 33200 North Railway Avenue, are run by BC Transit
BC Transit’s Central Fraser Valley route list includes Mission routes 31 Valley Connector, 32 West Heights, 33 Cedar Valley, 34 East Side, 35 Hatzic and 39 Shopper Shuttle

parts.t: From City of Mission, BC Government, TransLink, BC Transit and Fraser Valley Regional Library pages. Street addresses are the City’s.

blocks.text: City recreation centre Mission Leisure Centre

parts.t: Per the City, the hours are 5:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. Monday to Friday, 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. on Saturday and 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. on Sunday. Statutory holidays have shorter hours, so look at the City’s status page before heading out
The City’s upgrade page lists work on the leisure pool and hot tub, the main pool, a north arena, a curling arena, a weight room, a steam room and a sauna

A playground for children aged 0 to 5 and another for ages 6 to 12, plus outdoor fitness equipment, tennis courts and a lacrosse box, paved trails, picnic tables and a washroom. An off-leash dog area and a nine-hole disc golf course are there too
According to the City, the park hosts the Mission City Farmers Market during spring and summer, and it is also where the annual Lights On! Tree Lighting takes place

The park is getting a Japanese Tea House. On its project page the City lists 7871 Taulbut Street as the address, expects construction to start in October 2026, and plans an opening event for early 2027
The City says the Activity Hub Master Plan covers the 20-hectare Centennial Park and Leisure Centre corridor

blocks.text: City park Fraser River Heritage Park

parts.t: The City calls it Mission’s largest park, with walking trails, a picnic shelter, a gazebo and a rose garden. It is off 5th Avenue, east of Stave Lake Street

The City’s statement of significance says the park is on the site of St. Mary’s Mission, where the mission buildings were built from 1882 to 1885. The City lists it on its Heritage Conservation Register

items.t: The corner of Emiry Street and Brunton Court in Cedar Valley

parts.t: The City broke ground on July 6, 2026 on a 1.54-hectare (3.8-acre) park that will have a spray park, playground, sports courts, parking, walking trails and picnic areas
Under construction, so it is not open yet

The City’s Leisure Guide lists Griner Park (Cherry Ave.), Hatzic Park (Draper St.), Jack Poole Harbourside Park (Harbour Ave.), Wren Park (Silverhill Ave.), Tunbridge Common (Tunbridge Ave.) and Fenn Park (3rd Ave.)
The City says Jack Poole Harbourside Park is at Harbour Avenue and Abbott Street, with paved trails, picnic tables and a washroom
Per the FVRL page, the library opens 1 to 5 p.m. on Sunday, 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. Monday to Thursday, and 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Friday and Saturday. Holiday hours differ, so check ahead of a visit
It is the only FVRL branch in Mission

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Mission BC

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.

On June 1, 2026 the City adopted a new Official Community Plan, Bylaw 6405-2026. Bylaw 6350-2025 is repealed and replaced by it, and according to the City’s public notice the new plan is substantively the same one.
Before that, Bylaw 6350-2025 was adopted on May 20, 2025, and Bylaw 5670-2017 on January 8, 2018.

The 2025 plan’s land use designations include Downtown, Neighbourhood Centre, Mid-Rise Residential Plus, Mid-Rise Residential, Urban Residential Townhouse, Urban Residential (SSMUH), Suburban Residential, Rural Residential, Rural and Agriculture. The City’s March 2026 notice says the 2026 bylaw keeps the same land use framework and mapping.
The City’s housing report says its Bill 44 alignment amendments, adopted July 17, 2024, allow up to four units per lot within the Urban Growth Boundary.
The City’s housing report says its Transit-Oriented Areas bylaw was completed in summer 2024 to increase density near transit.
The Cedar Valley Local Area Plan (adopted November 18, 2019) covers the growth area around Cedar Street and Dewdney Trunk Road.
The City says the Activity Hub Master Plan covers the 20-hectare Centennial Park and Leisure Centre corridor.
The BC Government’s land use inventory describes Mission as largely steep, forested terrain on the north bank of the Fraser River.

Metro Vancouver’s flood response plan says the 1894 Fraser River flood is the largest on written record, with the water at Mission peaking at an estimated 7.92 metres, and that dikes and river structures were overtopped or breached along the river.
The City lists a Fraser River flood preparedness and response plan among its plans.
I found no City page that gives floodplain boundaries or flood construction levels street by street.

In the District of Mission Land Use Inventory (2011) from the BC Government, 1,539 hectares of Mission are recorded as Agricultural Land Reserve, which comes to nearly seven percent of the total land area of the District.
For a specific lot, send me the address and I’ll look up the zone and the plan designation.

How do I get around from Mission BC?

On weekdays TransLink runs the West Coast Express between Downtown Vancouver and Mission City, but only around the rush hours. Morning trips head west only, while the afternoon and evening ones head east only.
The West Coast Express page lists five westbound trains from Mission City, at 5:25, 5:55, 6:25, 6:55 and 7:25 a.m.
The Mission routes on BC Transit’s Central Fraser Valley list are 39 Shopper Shuttle, 35 Hatzic, 34 East Side, 33 Cedar Valley, 32 West Heights and 31 Valley Connector.
Which schools are in Mission BC?

The Province’s SD75 list has eight elementary schools in the central and western streets: Albert McMahon, Cherry Hill, École Christine Morrison, Edwin S. Richards, Hillside Traditional Academy, École Mission Central, West Heights and Windebank, all Kindergarten to 6.
SD75’s policy lists French Immersion at École Christine Morrison Elementary, École Mission Central Elementary, École Heritage Park Middle School and École Mission Senior Secondary.

The Province’s list shows École Mission Senior Secondary, at 32939 7th Avenue and serving Grades 10 to 12, as the district’s senior secondary school. There are plans for a replacement school on that site, with 1,500 seats, and the project is listed by Infrastructure BC as under construction.

The Mission Library, at 33247 Second Avenue, is the Fraser Valley Regional Library branch in Mission.
